To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gradient of the output of a deep neural network with respect to the inputs, which is a widely-used method for explaining the decision of the network, is often noisy and we propose a simple way to make it less noisy.

(a) noisy saliency is caused by the rectifier, (b) the rectifier can be replaced with a layer-wise thresholding function to alleviate the problem, and (c) our method, called Rectified Gradient (RG), is simple yet effective and superior to other attribution methods.
1) noisy saliency map is a common problem of all attribution methods and 2) rectifying gradient with respect to the output layer threshold is a simple yet effective solution to the problem.
